title: Per-model SLO lease, regional grace windows, and circuit-breaker handshake protocol
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a standardized protocol for short-term SLO borrowing (leases) between regions and a deterministic handshake for activating circuit-breakers during transient regional capacity loss. This causes fractured behavior across pinned low-latency endpoints: some degrade silently, others throttle aggressively, and customers see inconsistent error budgets and failover behavior.

Goal: Define and implement a "SLO Lease and Grace Window" policy plus a lightweight circuit-breaker handshake to coordinate regional failovers and load-shedding decisions per endpoint/model variant. The policy should: 1) enable short-lived borrowing of error budget across regions (leases) with clear reconciliation rules; 2) introduce configurable grace windows to avoid premature circuit tripping on short blips; 3) define the circuit-breaker handshake and signals exchanged between the routing layer and serving runtime; 4) provide operator-visible metrics and a migration plan for existing endpoints.

Scope: API endpoints (hosted + dedicated) and model variants that are latency-sensitive (tail P99 SLA & P95 throughput). Does NOT include on-prem Private deployments in the first tranche (treated separately due to network policy differences).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by SRE and Serving Runtime (sign-off from Maya Iqbal and Jordan Kim)
Protocol spec published in Confluence with sequence diagrams and example configurations

Implementation plan with a minimal proof-of-concept in staging that demonstrates: 1) cross-region lease grant/revoke flow; 2) grace-window suppression of circuit trigger for transient spikes; 3) observable metrics for lease usage and handshake traces
Automated tests for lease reconciliation (unit + integration) and simulated regional outage scenario (chaos test)
Runbook entry created for on-call remediation and manual lease revocation
implementation_notes: Lease model: token-based short leases (default 3 minutes, configurable 30s–10m) granted by a central lease arbiter service in the control plane
Grace windows: two-tier windows — soft grace (30s) which suppresses alerting and only increments transient counter; hard grace (3m) after which the circuit opens if thresholds breached

Circuit-breaker handshake: routing layer emits REQUEST_BLOCKED/REQUEST_OVERFLOW signals and runtime responds with OFFER_LEASE / REVOKE_LEASE messages. If OFFER_LEASE accepted, traffic is routed and a lease token attached to requests for traceability

Error budget reconciliation: leases decrement donor region’s escrowed ‘transferable_budget’ and increment recipient’s provisional budget. On revoke or expiration, reconciliation replays and credits back unused budget; overuse triggers automatic accounting and an audit log entry
Telemetry: new metrics - slo_lease_granted_total, slo_lease_rejected_total, slo_lease_expired_total, slo_lease_active_gauge, circuit_handshake_latency_ms, grace_window_suppressed_events_total
Backward compatibility: default behavior when control-plane lease arbiter unreachable = conservative fallback (no leases; local throttling only)
Security: leases signed (HMAC) by control-plane; tokens are ephemeral and carry only key id + expiry + endpoint key. No sensitive data in tokens
Config surface: per-endpoint config fields: enable_lease=true|false, lease_max_duration_seconds, soft_grace_seconds, hard_grace_seconds, accept_partial_lease=true|false
migration_plan: Phase 0 (design): collect a canonical set of latency-sensitive endpoints (via Console query) and publish recommended default values
Phase 1 (staging): implement arbiter + handshake in staging; run chaos test simulating AZ/regional packet loss and verify suppressed circuits during soft grace
Phase 2 (canary): enable for <10% traffic on dedicated tier for two weeks; monitor metrics and burn rate; iterate thresholds
Phase 3 (ramp): enable for remaining dedicated endpoints and select hosted routes with opt-in flags for customers
Phase 4 (post-rollout): add automated rollback in control plane if cumulative donor-region budget falls below safety floor
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: donor region may exhaust transferable budget causing cascading failures — Mitigation: safety floor per region and auto-revoke lowest-priority leases
Risk: increased control-plane dependency — Mitigation: leases are optional per-endpoint; conservative default when arbiter unreachable
Risk: lease accounting errors could create undetected SLO violations — Mitigation: implement idempotent reconciliation and audit logs; run daily reconciliation job in addition to event-driven updates
Risk: latency added by handshake — Mitigation: handshake is best-effort with optimistic routing; measure circuit_handshake_latency_ms and fall back after threshold
